description.narrative: (1) The government adopted a learning and development strategy for social protection through launching a community of practice (COP) on social protection to enhance knowledge and information exchange by social protection practitioners in September 2020. Process involved consultation with social partners (2) The Government enhanced and adopted Single Registry for Social Protection and Harmonized Social Assistance Targeting Tools to adopted disability indicators in March 2021 for use at the Household Listing Stage. (3) The government adopted the revised Kenya Social Protection Monitoring and Evaluation Framework in September 2020 enabling the harmonization of tools for comprehensive data collection and reporting on social protection at national, regional and global levels. The revised M&E Framework was developed in consultation with social partners and incorporates ILO principles and includes indicators to enhance reporting through the Social Security Inquiry system. (1) Through a joint initiative with UNICEF, WFP and SDG Fund, ILO was a part of the Technical Working Group on the development of the Community of Practice and provided technical inputs in the development process (2019 to 2020). The capacity of the Kenya School of Government is being enhanced to institutionalize social protection trainings utilizing the TRANSFORM methodology. (2) With the support from GLO/20/09/UNA; UNAIDS UBRAF Funding and in collaboration with World Food Programme, ILO (from August 2020 to March 2021), offered technical support to the State Department on Social Protection to incorporate disability indicators into the Enhanced Single Registry from the household listing stage thus ensuring that Persons with Disabilities (PWDs) are identified across all Social Assistance Programs countrywide. an advocacy brief for HIV-sensitive social protection was developed in July 2021 to enhance inclusive social protection programmes. (3) Through Joint SDG Fund on Social Protection (KEN19/52/UND); ILO provided technical guidance and inputs to the M&E Framework from April 2019 to September 2020.

description.narrative: (1) The government adopted an Issues Paper on occupational diseases and injuries compensation systems in September 2020. The action plan has been adopted following the consultation of a tripartite. The action plan adapts ILO principles to include social insurance based compensation system moving from employer liability, ‘no fault system', periodic payment system, tripartite governance system (2) The Government in March 2021 approved the establishment of Unemployment Insurance Fund, paving way for the processes of its establishment including feasibility and actuarial study; a multi-agency, tripartite committee established to support the process and a roadmap for its development is in place. (1) With the support from Joint SDG Fund on Social Protection (KEN19/52/UND) and other resources, the ILO supported the Directorate of Occupational Safety and Health Services to convene a high level dialogue forum in September 2020 on the establishment of an occupational diseases and illness compensation system through social insurance, the subsequent tripartite committee meetings (October 2020 to June 2021) to develop the issues paper/action plan and technical memorandum on the establishment of the compensation fund and provided technical inputs and guidance during this consensus building processes. (2) With the support from the government of Netherlands; KEN/19/51/NLD, ILO enhanced the capacity of the tripartite partners in March 2021 on unemployment protection through provision of technical guidance in the consensus building processes and in the development of the roadmap for the establishment of the Unemployment Insurance Fund. ILO is also supporting the government to conduct a feasibility and actuarial analysis.
